main_text.l: co,tum Mich.7.11. Armeniæ vero,quæ jam sub
Turcarum imperio est, duæ sunt partes; Major,
trâs Euphrate, quæ hodie Turcomannia, & Mi-
nor quæ cis Euphrate cui Cilicia contermina,
quæ etiam Armenis abundat,et Carmania à Tur-
cis vocatur.
83. Stephanus vult Armenos esse Phryges ge-
nere, eorumque linguam in multis imitari; Strabo
vero probabilius: τὸ τῶν Ἀρμενίων ἔθνος[?], καὶ τὸ τῆς Συρῶν, καὶ τῶν Ἀραβῶν, πολλὴν ὁμοφυλίαν ἐμφαίνειν, κατά τε τὴν διάλεκτον,
καὶ τὰς βίας, καὶ τὰς τῆς σωμάτων χρόας[?], καὶ μάλιστα καθὸ πλησιόχωροι εἰσι. Armenorum gentem, ut & Syrorum & Arabum
multum præ se ferre cognationis, dialecto, vita,
& corporum formâ, maximè cùm vicini sint.
Arabes enim Mesopotamiam penetrârunt &
Armeniæ vicina loca, & partim ex Syris,
& partim ex Phrygibus Armenos coaluisse
verisimile est, & ex gentium istarum lingua
tertiam conflatam esse. Syriacè olim scripsisse
Armenos videtur colligi posse ex Polyæni lib. 4.
ubi de Eumene dicitur, quod Ἐπιστολὴν προσ-ηνεγκεν[?]. παρὰ Ὀρόντου[?] σατράπου τῆς Ἀρμενίας
γεγραμμένην Συρίοις γράμμασι. Epistolam protulit quasi ab Oronte Armeniæ satrapa Syriacis
literis conscriptam. Unde colligere est Syris
& Armenis propter viciniam linguæ communes
literas fuisse.
84. Armeni postquam fidè Christi recepissent,
Patriarchæ Constantinopolitano subditi erat: cùm
verò Muhammedana impietas Orientem invasi-set,
& Saracenorum victoria Ecclesiarum ordine
& subordinationem Episcoporu[?],quâ sibi invicem
connexi

page.notes: Greek words are copied from the scan at small size; the marked letters (ἔθνος, σωμάτων χρόας, Ἐπιστολὴν προσ-ηνεγκεν, Ὀρόντου) are doubtful. The comma after "Episcoporu" is as printed and may be a damaged "m". "co,tum" at the top is a fragment continued from the previous page. The "connexi" line at the foot is the catchword, and the text ends with "sibi invicem". No marginal notes or stains are legible.
